slides.title: Medical Education Moves to Digital Channels
bullets: Same goal as the medical education plan: close real knowledge gaps
Non-promotional formative activities, now delivered online
Digital adds scale, flexible access, and personalization
Complements in-person training rather than replacing it

slides.title: Three Ways HCPs Learn Digitally
bullets: Live webinars gather dispersed audiences with real-time Q&A
Asynchronous videos, infographics and podcasts fit a busy schedule
Structured e-learning offers progressive modules with formal accreditation
Each format suits a different depth and availability

slides.title: Rigor and Independence Still Apply
bullets: Content must rest on balanced, evidence-based material
Same MLR review as any other scientific material
Must stay clearly separate from promotional content
Applies to design, labeling and distribution alike

slides.title: Personalization In-Person Can't Match
bullets: Format and depth adapt to each HCP's known profile
Modules sequence according to demonstrated knowledge level
Completion and interest are measured with precision
That data feeds the design of future content

slides.title: Recommend It, Then Build On It
bullets: Spot from field conversations which content fits a specific HCP
Recommend it as a starting point or a follow-up
Reinforces the omnichannel logic across every channel

takeaway.title: Digital medical education keeps the rigor of in-person training while adding scale and personalization
bullets: Webinars, asynchronous content and e-learning each serve a different need
MLR review and separation from promotion still apply online
MSLs connect field conversations to the right digital content
